name: Bandwa Gadrauhteis Greutungi

abilities.name: Flying Wedge
abilities.text: The unit moves into a flying wedge-shaped attack formation.

abilities.name: Trample
abilities.text: Charges are more effective for an extended time.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Guerrilla Deployment
attributes.text: This unit can deploy outside of the deployment zone.

attributes.name: Hide (scrub & forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in scrub and forest until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

attributes.name: Impetuous
attributes.text: This unit gets an extra morale bonus when eager.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

short: Warriors Greutungi; Gadrauhts - translates as warrior; Greutungi is one of the Goths; Bandwa - the original meaning of this word means «banner, flag», but it also applies to the military units having this banner, the number of which is similar to the late medieval Chorągiew (banner).
history: One of the simplest forms of one-armed catapult, the onager relied on twisted skeins of animal sinew which provided the power to hurl either rocks or shot. Inaccurate but powerful, it was an effective siege machine against buildings and fortifications, but was of far less use on the battlefield unless firing into massed infantry ranks. First mentioned by Philon of Byzantium in his treatise on ‘Mechanics’, the onager made use of a sling-like cradle attached to a firing arm. This arm was inserted, twisted, and propelled rocks or shot through torsion. As the firing arm was released, the sling-like cradle would unhook, firing the projectile. A padded beam was incorporated into the housing frame to restrain the arm. Larger machines could require as many as eight or ten crewmen, and the incredible recoil meant that they could not be easily or safely mounted on walls or towers. Quickly constructed wherever wood was readily available, onagers soon became a staple of ancient siege warfare.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
